election_name: November 3, 2026 U.S. Senate general and open primary election

www.sos.la.gov.es: la Secretaría de Estado de Louisiana

voterportal.sos.la.gov.en: the Louisiana Voter Portal (Louisiana Secretary of State)
voterportal.sos.la.gov.es: el buscador oficial de la Secretaría de Estado de Louisiana

reg_deadline.en: Registration closed Monday, October 5, 2026, in person, by mail or at an OMV office, and Tuesday, October 13, 2026, online.
reg_deadline.es: El registro cerró el lunes 5 de octubre de 2026 en persona, por correo o en una oficina de la OMV, y el martes 13 de octubre de 2026 en línea.
reg_deadline.quote: The deadline to register to vote in person, by mail, or at an OMV Office is October 5.

mail_request.en: Request your absentee ballot by 4:30 p.m. on Friday, October 30, 2026, online through the Voter Portal or in writing to your parish Registrar of Voters. Military and overseas voters, and voters who are in the hospital, have until 4:30 p.m. on Monday, November 2.
mail_request.es: Pide tu boleta de voto en ausencia a más tardar a las 4:30 p. m. del viernes 30 de octubre de 2026, en línea en el Voter Portal o por escrito al registrador de votantes de tu parroquia (Registrar of Voters). Los votantes militares y en el extranjero, y los votantes que están hospitalizados, tienen hasta las 4:30 p. m. del lunes 2 de noviembre.
mail_request.quote: General and Disabled Applications: Applicants must request a ballot by 4:30 p.m. CST on the 4th day before election day . Military, Overseas or Hospitalized Applications: Military personnel and/or their dependents; U.S. citizens residing outside the U.S.; or voters that are hospitalized must request their ballot by 4:30 p.m. CST on the day before election day .
mail_request.en_after: Absentee requests closed at 4:30 p.m. on October 30, 2026. Military and overseas voters, and voters who are in the hospital, have until 4:30 p.m. on Monday, November 2. Everyone else votes at their polling place on Election Day, 6 a.m. to 8 p.m.
mail_request.es_after: Las solicitudes de boleta de voto en ausencia cerraron a las 4:30 p. m. del 30 de octubre de 2026. Los votantes militares y en el extranjero, y los votantes que están hospitalizados, tienen hasta las 4:30 p. m. del lunes 2 de noviembre. Todos los demás votan en su lugar de votación el Día de las Elecciones, de 6 a. m. a 8 p. m.
mail_request.notes: The 4th day before Nov 3 is Oct 30, matching https://www.sos.la.gov/elections-voting/election-dates ('The deadline to request an absentee ballot is October 30 by 4:30 p.m (other than military and overseas voters).'). Hospitalized applications need the documentation described on the application.

mail_return.en: Your parish Registrar of Voters must receive your voted ballot by 4:30 p.m. on Monday, November 2, 2026, the day before Election Day. Military, overseas and hospitalized voters have until 8 p.m. on Election Day.
mail_return.es: La oficina del registro de votantes de tu parroquia (Registrar of Voters) debe recibir tu boleta votada a más tardar a las 4:30 p. m. del lunes 2 de noviembre de 2026, el día antes del Día de las Elecciones. Los votantes militares, en el extranjero u hospitalizados tienen hasta las 8 p. m. del Día de las Elecciones.
mail_return.quote: The deadline for a Registrar of Voters to receive a voted absentee ballot is November 2 by 4:30 p.m. (other than military and overseas voters).

early_hours.en: Early voting runs 8:30 a.m. to 6 p.m. each day. There's no early voting on Sunday, October 25.
early_hours.es: La votación anticipada es de 8:30 a. m. a 6 p. m. cada día. No hay votación anticipada el domingo 25 de octubre.
early_hours.quote: Early voting is October 20-27 (excluding Sunday, October 25) from 8:30 a.m.-6 p.m.
early_hours.en_after: Early voting ended October 27. Vote at your polling place on Election Day, 6 a.m. to 8 p.m.
early_hours.es_after: La votación anticipada terminó el 27 de octubre. Vota en tu lugar de votación el Día de las Elecciones, de 6 a. m. a 8 p. m.

cure.en: If your Registrar of Voters contacts you about a problem with your absentee envelope, such as a missing signature, witness signature or mother's maiden name, go to their office in person by 4:30 p.m. on Monday, November 2, 2026, to fix it. Or ask for a replacement ballot, which has to reach the registrar by that same deadline.
cure.es: Si el registrador de votantes (Registrar of Voters) te contacta por un problema con el sobre de tu boleta de voto en ausencia, como que falte tu firma, la firma del testigo o el apellido de soltera de tu madre, ve en persona a su oficina a más tardar a las 4:30 p. m. del lunes 2 de noviembre de 2026 para corregirlo. O pide una boleta de reemplazo, que tiene que llegarle al registrador antes de esa misma fecha límite.
cure.quote: If you are contacted by the Registrar of Voters about a deficiency with your absentee by mail certificate, you must appear in person at their Registrar of Voters office by no later than 4:30 p.m. the day before the election to cure the certificate deficiency. Alternatively, you may request a replacement ballot from the registrar. The same deadline applies for returning the replacement ballot.

in_person.en: You don't need a reason to vote early. Vote in person at a designated early voting location in your parish, just like on Election Day. On Election Day, vote at the polling place listed on your voter information card.
in_person.es: No necesitas una razón para votar por anticipado. Vota en persona en un lugar de votación anticipada designado en tu parroquia, igual que el Día de las Elecciones. El Día de las Elecciones, vota en el lugar de votación que aparece en tu tarjeta de información de votante.
in_person.quote: You do not need a reason to vote early! All voters may vote early, just like they are voting on election day.

first_time.en: Registered online or by mail and never voted in your parish? You have to vote in person the first time, during early voting or on Election Day. Exceptions include voters 65 and older, military and overseas voters, homebound voters with a disability, students who send a copy of their student ID or fee bill, voters who verify their identity at the registrar's office before the election, and voters who already voted in another parish where they were registered.
first_time.es: ¿Te registraste en línea o por correo y nunca has votado en tu parroquia? Tienes que votar en persona la primera vez, durante la votación anticipada o el Día de las Elecciones. Las excepciones incluyen a votantes de 65 años o más, votantes militares y en el extranjero, votantes con una discapacidad que no pueden salir de casa, estudiantes que envían una copia de su identificación estudiantil o de su recibo de matrícula (fee bill), votantes que verifican su identidad en la oficina del registrador antes de la elección y votantes que ya votaron en otra parroquia donde estaban registrados.
first_time.quote: If you registered to vote online or by mail and you have not previously voted in the parish, you are not eligible to vote absentee and must vote in person the first time, either during early voting or on election day. Exceptions include: military or overseas citizens; senior citizens (65+); people who are homebound because of a disability; students, who submit a copy of student ID or fee bill with the request; citizens who appear in the registrar of voters office before the election to verify identity; participants in the state's address confidentiality program; and a person who was registered to vote in another parish and previously voted in the other parish
first_time.en_after: Registered online or by mail and never voted in your parish? You have to vote in person the first time, so vote at your polling place on Election Day. Exceptions include voters 65 and older, military and overseas voters, homebound voters with a disability, students who send a copy of their student ID or fee bill, voters who verify their identity at the registrar's office before the election, and voters who already voted in another parish where they were registered.
first_time.es_after: ¿Te registraste en línea o por correo y nunca has votado en tu parroquia? Tienes que votar en persona la primera vez, así que vota en tu lugar de votación el Día de las Elecciones. Las excepciones incluyen a votantes de 65 años o más, votantes militares y en el extranjero, votantes con una discapacidad que no pueden salir de casa, estudiantes que envían una copia de su identificación estudiantil o de su recibo de matrícula (fee bill), votantes que verifican su identidad en la oficina del registrador antes de la elección y votantes que ya votaron en otra parroquia donde estaban registrados.

locator_label.en: Louisiana Voter Portal (Louisiana Secretary of State)
locator_label.es: Buscador oficial de lugares de votación (Secretaría de Estado de Louisiana)

rule.en: Your voter information card lists your polling place. You can also look it up in the Louisiana Voter Portal or call your parish Registrar of Voters. Early voting sites for your parish are in the Voter Portal too.
rule.es: Tu tarjeta de información de votante dice cuál es tu lugar de votación. También puedes buscarlo en el buscador oficial del estado (Louisiana Voter Portal) o llamar a la oficina del registro de votantes de tu parroquia (Registrar of Voters). Los lugares de votación anticipada de tu parroquia también están en ese buscador.
rule.quote: Use the Louisiana Voter Portal to find where you vote on election day, or call your parish Registrar of Voters Office. Your voter information card received by mail lists your polling place.

en: U.S. military ID card with your name and picture
Any other recognized picture ID with your name and signature
es: Tarjeta de identificación especial de Louisiana (Louisiana Special ID)
Licencia de conducir digital en la aplicación oficial del estado (LA Wallet)
Identificación militar de EE. UU. con tu nombre y foto
Cualquier otra identificación con foto reconocida que tenga tu nombre y tu firma
accepted.quote: When you go to the polls to cast your vote in an election, be sure to take one of the following:

expired.notes: No rule on expired IDs found on sos.la.gov.

without.en: No photo ID? You can still vote. Answer questions that confirm who you are, then sign a voter identification affidavit. A voter who votes this way can be challenged under the law. A free Louisiana Special ID is available at the Office of Motor Vehicles when you show your voter information card.
without.es: ¿No tienes identificación con foto? Todavía puedes votar. Contesta las preguntas que confirman quién eres y luego firma una declaración jurada de identificación de votante (voter identification affidavit). Un votante que vota así puede ser impugnado según la ley. Puedes obtener gratis una Louisiana Special ID en la Oficina de Vehículos Motorizados (Office of Motor Vehicles) si muestras tu tarjeta de información de votante.
without.quote: A voter without photo ID may vote after completing the affidavit but is subject to challenge by law.
without.notes: Identifying questions: https://www.sos.la.gov/elections-voting/ways-to-vote (Oct 28): 'or you may vote by affidavit after correctly answering identifying information before voting.'

who.en: In Louisiana you need a reason to vote by mail, unless you're a military or overseas voter. You can apply if you:
who.es: En Louisiana necesitas una razón para votar por correo, a menos que seas votante militar o en el extranjero. Puedes pedirla si:
who.quote: In Louisiana, you must have a reason to be eligible to vote by mail, unless you are a military or overseas voter.

en: have a physical disability, or are homebound and can't vote without help
will be outside Louisiana or your parish during early voting and on Election Day
will be working offshore during early voting and on Election Day
are a student, instructor or professor living outside your parish, or their spouse or dependent
are clergy assigned outside your parish, or their spouse or dependent
moved more than 100 miles from your old parish seat after registration closed
will be hospitalized on Election Day and couldn't vote early, under the rules on the application
are in jail and not serving a felony sentence
are involuntarily confined for mental treatment outside your parish
will be a sequestered juror on Election Day
are in the Secretary of State's Address Confidentiality Program
es: tienes una discapacidad física, o no puedes salir de casa y no puedes votar sin ayuda
vas a estar fuera de Louisiana o de tu parroquia durante la votación anticipada y el Día de las Elecciones
vas a estar trabajando en altamar durante la votación anticipada y el Día de las Elecciones
eres estudiante, instructor o profesor y vives fuera de tu parroquia, o eres su cónyuge o dependiente
eres miembro del clero asignado fuera de tu parroquia, o eres su cónyuge o dependiente
te mudaste a más de 100 millas de la sede de tu antigua parroquia después de que cerró el registro
vas a estar hospitalizado el Día de las Elecciones y no pudiste votar por anticipado, según las reglas de la solicitud
estás en la cárcel y no cumples una condena por un delito grave
estás internado involuntariamente para tratamiento mental fuera de tu parroquia
vas a ser jurado aislado por un tribunal el Día de las Elecciones
estás en el programa de confidencialidad de domicilio de la Secretaría de Estado (Address Confidentiality Program)
who_list.quote: If you are 65 years of age or older you may apply through a Senior Citizen Application and, once accepted by the registrar of voters, absentee vote.

witness.en: Sign the certificate envelope and add your mother's maiden name (write "unknown" if you don't know it). A witness signs too and prints their name and address. Unless they're your immediate family, a person can witness only one voter's envelope.
witness.es: Firma el sobre del certificado y agrega el apellido de soltera de tu madre (escribe "unknown" si no lo sabes). Un testigo también firma y escribe en letra de molde su nombre y dirección. Si no es de tu familia inmediata, una persona puede ser testigo del sobre de un solo votante.
witness.quote: Section B on the back of the Certificate Envelope with the following information: voter’s signature, mother’s maiden name (if you do not know your mother’s maiden name, write “unknown”), witnesses' signature, witnesses' printed name, and the address of the witness.
witness.notes: Witness limit: R.S. 18:1306, https://www.legis.la.gov/Legis/Law.aspx?d=81340 (Oct 28): 'No person except the immediate family member of the voter, as defined in this Code, shall witness more than one certificate of a voter.' Military and overseas voters don't need a witness (same section).

cure.en: Your Registrar of Voters checks each envelope for a missing voter signature, witness signature or mother's maiden name. If one is missing, they mail you a notice, and call or email if they have your contact details. Fix it in person at their office or ask for a replacement ballot.
cure.es: La oficina del registro de votantes (Registrar of Voters) revisa cada sobre por si falta la firma del votante, la firma del testigo o el apellido de soltera de tu mamá. Si falta algo, te manda un aviso por correo, y te llama o te escribe si tiene tus datos. Corrígelo en persona en esa oficina o pide una boleta de reemplazo.
cure.quote: Upon receipt of an absentee by mail certificate with one or more of the above identified deficiencies, the Registrar of Voters will immediately mail a written notice of the certificate deficiency to the voter to give them an opportunity to cure the deficiency.

dropbox.en: Return your ballot by mail or commercial carrier, by fax if you ask the registrar, or by hand to your Registrar of Voters' office. Someone else can hand deliver it for you if they sign a statement that you allowed it. Except for immediate family, no one can turn in more than one voter's ballot.
dropbox.es: Devuelve tu boleta por correo o por un servicio de mensajería comercial, por fax si se lo pides al registrador, o en mano en la oficina del registrador de votantes (Registrar of Voters). Otra persona puede entregarla por ti si firma una declaración de que tú lo autorizaste. Salvo tu familia inmediata, nadie puede entregar la boleta de más de un votante.
dropbox.quote: If delivered by other than the voter, a commercial courier, or the United States Postal Service, the registrar shall require that the person making such delivery sign a statement, prepared by the secretary of state, certifying that the person has the authorization and consent of the voter to hand deliver the marked ballot. ... No person except the immediate family of the voter, as defined in this Code, shall submit by any means or send for delivery by the United States Postal Service or commercial courier more than one marked ballot per election to the registrar.
dropbox.notes: R.S. 18:1308(B), read Oct 28. Replaces 'Only you or an immediate family member can hand deliver it', which follows the SOS Ways to Vote summary ('A voter or immediate family member of the voter may deliver the ballot') but not the statute. Hand delivery goes to the registrar's principal or branch office, or an early voting site during early voting (18:1308(B)(2)).

gear.en: Leave the campaign shirts and buttons at home. Never wear, hand out or display anything for or against a candidate, proposition or party on the ballot. Every polling place has a 600-foot campaign-free zone.
gear.es: Deja en casa las camisetas y botones de campaña. Nunca lleves puesto, repartas ni muestres nada a favor o en contra de un candidato, una propuesta o un partido que aparezca en la boleta. Todos los lugares de votación tienen una zona libre de campaña de 600 pies.
gear.quote: When voting, never wear, hand out, or display anything advocating for or against any candidate, proposition, or political party appearing on the ballot in the election. All polling places have a 600 foot campaign free zone.

phone.notes: No phone or ballot photo rule found on sos.la.gov (Ways to Vote and the voting FAQs). docs/faq-sources.json also left the Louisiana selfie answer null.

line.en: Polls close at 8 p.m. If you're in line at 8 p.m., you have the right to vote.
line.es: Los lugares de votación cierran a las 8 p. m. Si estás en la fila a las 8 p. m., tienes derecho a votar.
line.quote: Polls close at 8 p.m. All voters in line at 8 p.m. have the right to vote.

tradition.en: Louisiana's 2026 I voted sticker has art by New Orleans artist Terrance Osborne. He said he pictured what Louisiana would look like if you could see its sound. It's the state's sixth I voted sticker and the fifth Louisiana artist in a series that started in 2016 with George Rodrigue's Blue Dog.
tradition.es: El sticker de I voted de Louisiana para 2026 tiene arte de Terrance Osborne, artista de New Orleans. Él dijo que imaginó cómo se vería Louisiana si se pudiera ver su sonido. Es el sexto sticker de I voted del estado y el quinto artista de Louisiana en una serie que empezó en 2016 con el Blue Dog de George Rodrigue.
tradition.quote: The artwork for this year’s sticker was created by New Orleans artist Terrance Osborne, who also attended the unveiling. Osborne said that his inspiration for the art was the imagery of what Louisiana would look like if you could see its sound. “Today’s unveiling marks Louisiana’s 6th ‘I Voted’ sticker and the 5th Louisiana artist featured as part of the series,” Secretary Landry said.
tradition.notes: July 28, 2026 release, read Oct 28. Was 'sixth artist-designed sticker'; the release says sixth sticker, fifth Louisiana artist. 'Painted' changed to 'has art by' (release: 'created'). The release doesn't describe distribution.

provisional.en: If your name isn't on the voter list, you can vote a paper provisional ballot for federal offices only, after certifying in writing that you're eligible. It counts only if you're registered in that parish. Check whether it counted with the provisional voter search, at least seven days after the election.
provisional.es: Si tu nombre no aparece en la lista de votantes, puedes votar con una boleta provisional de papel solo para cargos federales, después de certificar por escrito que puedes votar. Cuenta solo si estás registrado en esa parroquia. Revisa si se contó en el buscador oficial de boletas provisionales (provisional voter search), por lo menos siete días después de la elección.
provisional.quote: You must be a registered voter in the parish where you vote and eligible to vote in the election for federal office for your vote to be counted.

line.en: You can still vote. Every voter in line at 8 p.m. has the right to vote.
line.es: Todavía puedes votar. Todos los votantes que están en la fila a las 8 p. m. tienen derecho a votar.
line.quote: All voters in line at 8 p.m. have the right to vote.

track.en: Track your absentee ballot in the Louisiana Voter Portal.
track.es: Sigue tu boleta de voto en ausencia en el buscador oficial del estado (Louisiana Voter Portal).
track.quote: You can track the status of your absentee ballot here.

late_mail.en: It may be. Your parish Registrar of Voters must receive it by 4:30 p.m. on Monday, November 2, the day before Election Day, and a postmark doesn't count. You or an immediate family member can still hand it in at the registrar's office by then. Military, overseas and hospitalized voters have until 8 p.m. on Election Day.
late_mail.es: Puede que sí. El registrador de votantes de tu parroquia (parish Registrar of Voters) debe recibirla a más tardar a las 4:30 p. m. del lunes 2 de noviembre, el día antes de las elecciones, y el matasellos no cuenta. Tú o un familiar directo todavía pueden entregarla en la oficina del registrador antes de esa hora. Los votantes militares, en el extranjero u hospitalizados tienen hasta las 8 p. m. del Día de las Elecciones.
late_mail.quote: General and Disabled Voters: Voted ballots must be received by your parish Registrar of Voters by 4:30 p.m. CST on the day before election day . ... By Hand Delivery: A voter or immediate family member of the voter may deliver the ballot to the registrar of voters (a signed statement must be completed upon delivery by anyone other that the voter, certifying their relationship to the voter)
late_mail.notes: Pass 2 Oct 30, read by curl. Nov 2 date also on sos.la.gov/elections-voting/election-dates ('November 2 by 4:30 p.m.'). Hand delivery also in R.S. 18:1308(B) (mail.dropbox).

The sos.la.gov pages link the Voter Portal as 'voterportal.--environment--.sos.la.gov' (an unfilled template placeholder); the file uses https://voterportal.sos.la.gov/, which loads the Voter Portal: Search page. EARLY VOTING DATES FOR THE LEAD (states.js has LA unchecked): Tuesday, October 20 to Tuesday, October 27, 2026, no voting Sunday, October 25, 8:30 a.m. to 6 p.m. Sources: (1) https://www.sos.la.gov/elections-voting/election-dates: 'Early voting is October 20-27 (excluding Sunday, October 25) from 8:30 a.m.-6 p.m.' (2) https://www.sos.la.gov/elections-voting/ways-to-vote, same sentence under 'November 3, 2026', and 'The registrars of voters will open their offices from 8:30 a.m. to 6 p.m. for each day of early voting.' The November 3 ballot is the U.S. Senate general and the open primary; a December 12, 2026 election follows. Expired-ID and phone rules not found.

hours.en: Polling places are open 6 a.m. to 8 p.m. local time.
hours.es: Los lugares de votación abren de 6 a. m. a 8 p. m., hora local.
hours.quote: On election day, the polls are open from 6 a.m.-8 p.m.
